name: Iberism
summary: Iberism holds that Portugal and Spain, with their shared history, near-kindred languages and the precedent of the 1580-1640 Iberian Union, should be politically united. The nineteenth-century movement ran from Sinibaldo de Mas's plan for a customs and monetary union under one monarchy to federal-republican schemes by Pi y Margall, Castelar and Teofilo Braga; modern Iberist parties favour a gradual confederation inside the European Union. It is mainly a territorial and constitutional project and takes few positions on economic or social questions.
scope: Mainstream Iberism as a political project: the nineteenth-century movement (Mas's La Iberia, 1851-55; the federal-republican strand of Pi y Margall, Castelar, Garrido and Braga; the Catalan and Galician Iberists such as Maragall) and the present-day confederal Iberists (Iber, Movimento Partido Iberico, the Lisbon Declaration of 2016). Monarchist-fusionist and federal-republican strands split on the form of government, which is recorded as neutral. Excludes Francoist and Salazarist rhetoric about the peninsula, Pan-Iberism extended to Latin America beyond what the Lisbon Declaration states, and Iberian cultural-identity usages with no political union aim. Most social and economic statements are inferred, so are marked low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Sinibaldo de Mas
keyFigures.role: Spanish diplomat and author of La Iberia (1851), the most-read Iberist work of the nineteenth century.

keyFigures.name: Francisco Pi y Margall
keyFigures.role: Federal republican and president of the First Spanish Republic, listed among Iberist figures and writing of the day both peoples would be united in one nation.

keyFigures.name: Miguel de Unamuno
keyFigures.role: Spanish writer named among the cultural Iberists, who framed union as a spiritual one of peninsular and overseas peoples.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Iberism has no health program; 19th-century progressive and federal-republican strands stressed social reform, so mild support is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not an Iberist topic and the idea postdates the 19th-century texts; mild support is inferred from the social-reform emphasis of Pi y Margall and Garrido.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mas argued for removing customs barriers and merging the two countries' commercial interests, a market-integration stance, but he did not write a general theory of markets versus the state.

public-ownership.rationale: Sources give no Iberist line on ownership; the liberal-monarchist and the socialist-federal strands would split, so it is left neutral.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Never addressed as an Iberist demand; bourgeois fusionists and social federalists would differ.

unions-good.rationale: Iberism is a territorial project; the anarchist and socialist currents that took it up were pro-union but liberal and monarchist Iberists were not.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Iberist family spans propertied liberals (Mas) and federal republicans critical of latifundismo, so no common line exists.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; no basis to lean either way.

cut-welfare.rationale: Federal-republican Iberists were tied to social reform, so cutting welfare is unlikely, but this is inferred, not documented.

worker-ownership.rationale: Only the anarchist and socialist currents of Iberism, such as the FAI, would favour it; mainstream strands never took a view.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No documented Iberist position; liberal and security-minded adherents would split.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; no basis for a lean.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Never addressed; the issue does not map onto Iberist concerns.

strong-leader.rationale: Federal and republican Iberism favoured decentralised, pacted government, and Mas wanted union under a constitutional crown; a bypass-the-legislature leader is unlikely to appeal.

state-harmful.rationale: Iberism proposes building a larger state; even the anarchist current (FAI) is an exception, not the mainstream, which wants a federation or confederation with institutions.

empower-police-military.rationale: Mas argued union would let a strong Iberian government cut the standing army and its cost, so more military authority runs against his case.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Sex work law never figures in Iberist writing, which concerns peninsular union; no lean can be derived.

decide-locally.rationale: Federal Iberism proposed unions built from municipalities up (Pi y Margall) and of nationalities, and was used against Castilian centralism, so local decision is favoured.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not documented; progressive and republican strands usually backed penal reform, so mild support is inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: The sources give no stance; conservative-monarchist and liberal-republican Iberists would differ.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic for the historical texts; modern Iberist groups have no recorded line.

abortion-legal.rationale: No documented position for any Iberist strand.

more-religion-public.rationale: Mas called the Portuguese and Spanish religion shared and rather harmonised, but the movement was driven by liberal and republican currents, not clericalism; mild disagreement is inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Racial redress is outside Iberism's concerns, a project about uniting Portugal and Spain; left neutral.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not an Iberist topic and anachronistic.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Iberists prize the peninsula's shared culture and also its distinct peoples, but no source frames it as preserving one national culture; the nation in question is itself being redefined.

gradual-change.rationale: Current Iberist parties describe a stepwise process measured in centuries (a ministry, a joint bank, a league), and Mas urged union by peaceful, legal means.

reduce-immigration.rationale: No source addresses immigration; the project favours open borders and shared citizenship between neighbours, so restriction is unlikely.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Modern Iberists want to stay in the EU and gain weight in Brussels; support for stronger international bodies is inferred from that.

free-trade.rationale: Mas wanted a customs union with a single tariff and commercial law, and Latino Coelho's preface wanted a full zollverein; Iberism is built around removing trade barriers between the two states.

nation-first.rationale: Iberism rejects separate national egoism; Mas criticised governments that perpetuate national egoism under the cover of patriotism, and modern parties seek shared interests within the EU.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed by any Iberist source.

open-borders.rationale: Iberists celebrate the end of the Spain-Portugal border controls under Schengen and Mas wanted the frontier customs barriers abolished; a general open-borders view is inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; the economic-integration case rests on growth, so growth limits are unlikely.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear energy is an energy-policy question the 19th-century and modern Iberist sources do not take up.

revolution-justified.rationale: Mas called revolution a transitional state, not the norm, while some republican and anarchist Iberists (1820s secret societies, FAI) were revolutionary; the strands split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Republican and federal strands stressed popular sovereignty; no source says more.

central-planning.rationale: Mas's economics were liberal-commercial; central planning is inferred as unlikely.

socialized-markets.rationale: Only the socialist and anarchist currents would care; no common line.

land-value-tax.rationale: A single land tax is not part of any Iberist programme in the sources read.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation is absent from Iberist sources; liberal and social-federal strands would differ.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Iberists such as Sinibaldo de Mas wanted the tariff and fiscal barriers between Spain and Portugal removed in a customs union; that argues against internal protection, not against a common external tariff, so the opposition is mild.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Mas wanted joint railways and canals, which implies public works, but no general investment doctrine is stated.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Federal republicans attacked latifundismo, but no Iberist-wide land doctrine exists.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Only anarchist currents would favour; mainstream Iberism wants a common currency, not abolition of money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Íber proposes a joint Iberian Central Bank as an early step, so abolishing central banks goes against its program.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised employer-worker bodies are a fascist-era model, and the Salazar and Franco regimes that used them were hostile to Iberism; no Iberist programme includes them.

one-party-rule.rationale: Iberism has been republican, federal, liberal and anarchist; Estado Novo and Francoism, the one-party regimes, were hostile to it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Documented split: Mas and progresista liberals wanted union under one constitutional monarchy, while democrats and federal republicans saw monarchy as tied to oligarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: The dominant Iberist strands were liberal, democratic and republican, and modern Iberist parties work through elections.

direct-votes.rationale: Not documented as an Iberist demand.

workers-councils.rationale: Only some anarchist and socialist strands would favour it; not part of mainstream Iberism.

right-to-secede.rationale: Iberism seeks union and some strands (Pi y Margall) built it on voluntary pacts, but no source asserts a right to leave, so a mild no is inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Republican and democratic Iberism rejects inherited superiority; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: Mas stressed peaceful legal union, but revolutionary Iberists existed, so adherents split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Mas argued union would end the rivalry and armed forces' burden of the two peoples, and Latino Coelho's preface praised fusion as disarming two armies.

separate-church-state.rationale: Liberal republican Iberists leaned secular, conservative ones did not; no common line.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: No source supports it and the movement is mostly liberal.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Unaddressed; inferred from the statist federal design.

military-superiority.rationale: Mas wanted a smaller army and thought Iberia would be strong but not militarised.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Iberism joins Castilian, Portuguese, Catalan and Galician peoples as a federation of nationalities, not an ethnic nation state.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Only socialist and anarchist Iberists would affirm it.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Iberism has no economic-equality doctrine; its social-reform wing would favour opportunity measures but nothing says outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land rights are not an Iberist theme, though its overseas-peoples cultural strand (Unamuno) is about shared heritage, not land authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not discussed; Mas treated colonies as assets to develop.

civilizational-union.rationale: Mas appealed to shared origin, language, religion and customs as grounds for peninsular union, and Unamuno's cultural Iberism extended to overseas peoples.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Moral status of self-interest is not treated; Mas defended union on the material interests of both peoples without a moral claim about egoism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Liberal and republican Iberism rests on rights and popular sovereignty; inferred, not stated.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics is outside Iberism's concerns.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is not discussed; Mas counted peninsular population as an asset of union.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Mas championed railways, canals and commerce as the engines of peninsular prosperity.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Mas wanted railways and canals linking the peninsula, but no general doctrine of disruptive technological change exists.

restore-past-order.rationale: Iberism looks forward to a new peninsular union; its historical precedent (1580-1640) is cited but not as a lost order to restore, and Mas wrote of a regenerative future.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Mas pitched union on material advantages, not party ideology (he said the work served interests, not a party), but no general rule is stated.

direct-action.rationale: Iberist parties run in elections and Mas urged legal union; some anarchist strands differ.

means-match-ends.rationale: Iberist writers prefer peaceful legal means (Mas) but state no general principle that methods mirror ends.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Only socialist-anarchist currents would support it.

production-for-use.rationale: Only socialist-anarchist currents would support it.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Only socialist currents would affirm it; Mas's liberal commercial case would not.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Iberism is federal and democratic-republican; no Marxist-Leninist strand is documented.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Mas blamed national egoism and dynastic rivalry for wars, not capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Iberism proposes a unified state and treasury; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Mill-style limits on state power are not an Iberist topic; sources are about territorial and economic union.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Iberism is framed around rights of nationalities and peoples within a federation, so rights belonging only to individuals is unlikely.

conscription.rationale: Mas wanted to cut the standing army; conscription is inferred as unattractive.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not discussed; Iberism is a project of political union, so inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: The citizen-as-customer idea is absent; Iberism proposes a larger shared state, not a market in jurisdictions, so a mild no is inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social federalists such as Pi y Margall and Garrido stressed social reform; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Claims about media and universities ruling politics are absent from Iberist sources.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inference: Iberism argued from shared peninsular origin and language and never made claims about genetic racial ability; the sources do not discuss it.

organic-representation.rationale: Not part of Iberist programs; inferred.

total-state.rationale: Estado Novo and Francoism, totalising regimes, were hostile to Iberism; its strands are liberal, federal or anarchist.

national-rebirth.rationale: Mas called union the one great idea that could regenerate the peninsula after the miseries of the Spanish revolution.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Iberism seeks union and, in Mas's plan, adding the Balearics, Andorra and parts of France; but it is peaceful union, so expansion by force is not endorsed.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oaths of loyalty are entirely alien to a liberal-federal movement.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom has no place in Iberism, whose liberal and republican strands were hostile to feudal remnants.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology is not addressed by Iberist sources.

universal-morality.rationale: Moral universalism is not addressed in Iberist sources.

single-common-good.rationale: Iberist federalists accept plural nationalities and interests; the sources do not take up the common-good question.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Israel question lies wholly outside Iberism.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return is not an Iberist issue.

revive-national-language.rationale: Galician reintegrationism is mentioned, but no Iberist-wide line on reviving languages exists.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Only socialist currents would back it.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not part of Iberist sources.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Mas wanted reduced military spending and thrift, but no deficit doctrine is stated.

economic-freedom.rationale: Mas coupled political regeneration with free commerce, but no source states the freedom linkage as a principle.

rule-by-example.rationale: Moral example of rulers as a substitute for law is a Confucian idea; Iberist constitutionalists rely on legal union (Mas, legal and peaceful), so a mild no is inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Documented tension: Iberism uses the language of nationalities' rights (Catalan, Galician) against Castilian centralism but seeks to merge states.

force-without-un.rationale: Mas wanted union peaceful; inferred pacific orientation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Iberist sources do not weigh reason against faith; Mas listed shared religion among the ties between the two peoples.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Iberism seeks shared citizenship across the border; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare is not addressed in Iberist sources.

class-collaboration.rationale: Mas pitched union as in the interest of both peoples and not of a party; inferred cooperation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Foreign to Iberism, which values shared culture and heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Modern Iberist declarations speak of an Iberofone space but not of fronts against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: A national-line workers movement is not Iberist; anarchist Iberists (FAI) organised across both states, so a mild no is inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Gender roles in law are not addressed by Iberist sources.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Segregation has no place in a movement uniting kindred peoples across a border.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Only the socialist/anarchist current would assent.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Fossil-fuel policy is not covered in Iberist sources.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not discussed; Iberism stresses diversity within union.

elite-replacement.rationale: The replacement conspiracy is alien to Iberism.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in the Iberist texts read.

national-mission.rationale: Latino Coelho's preface envisages Iberian fusion as a step to a European federation; no mission to spread a government form.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Structural-patriarchy analysis is not part of Iberist writing.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Mas attacked governments that perpetuate national egoism, but no corruption theme is documented.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for state killings is not an Iberist question; Franco-era memory politics are separate from the doctrine.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Iberism proposes building a larger federal state with joint institutions.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Foreign to Iberism, which unites related peoples.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Inferred from the liberal and republican commitments of the main strands.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Whether settler states are colonial is not covered by Iberist sources.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Uniform civil law across religions is not an Iberist topic; both countries are Catholic-majority.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious conversion law is not an Iberist topic; a mild no is inferred from the liberal strands.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle slaughter law is alien to Iberism; mild no inferred from the bullfighting-and-meat culture of the peninsula.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Church-school relations are not specified in Iberist sources; liberal and conservative adherents would split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state doctrine is not Iberist.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Mas called for a peaceful, legal union and the republican strand built federation by pacts from municipalities up; the 1820s and Íber models stress voluntary union.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mas argued for removing tariffs and merging commercial interests, not for mercantilist surpluses.

population-transfer.rationale: Foreign to Iberism, which seeks peaceful union.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Mas stressed peaceful and legal union, but the principle itself is not stated.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Latino Coelho's preface treats fusion of peoples as progress through reconciliation, not struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Militant democracy is not discussed in the Iberist sources.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Mas's case against foreign domination (Britain's protectorate over Portugal) comes close but no republican freedom theory is stated.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional and republican strands favour divided powers; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninist vanguardism is not part of Iberism; its anarchist and federal currents opposed it.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Preferential concern for the poor appears in social-federal writing but is not a stated Iberist principle.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public-housing sales are not part of Iberist sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is not discussed in the Iberist sources.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Malthusian explanations of poverty are not discussed in Iberist sources.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Iberism assumes a federation of distinct nationalities and languages can cohere; Íber's leader cites Switzerland's four languages.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not part of the Iberist proposals; a mild no is inferred from the elective federal-republican tradition.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price control is not an Iberist issue; Mas's commercial argument leans free-trade, so adherents would be split.

party-controls-media.rationale: Authoritarian media control fits the regimes hostile to Iberism, not Iberism itself.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the army is a single-party-state device, foreign to a federal and liberal movement.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from shared-citizenship ideal.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of representatives is not addressed in Iberist sources.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Iberism is itself a proposal to pool or merge the sovereignty of two states, and current parties pursue it inside the EU, wanting more weight in Brussels; Mas's text calls for a European republic of nations.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not discussed; monarchist and republican strands differ.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside the Iberist programme.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by clerics is incompatible with liberal and republican Iberism.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is a Leninist doctrine; Iberism had pacifist tendencies against inter-state war but no such doctrine.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral censorship of art is not an Iberist theme; mild no inferred from its liberal origins.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials is not documented as an Iberist demand.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Mas wanted freedom from foreign (British, French) influence but not alliance abolition.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Banning rental housing is alien to every Iberist strand.

people-in-arms.rationale: A citizen militia in place of a professional army is not stated; Mas wanted a smaller army but not abolition of professionals.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rural moral superiority is not an Iberist idea.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Mas and later Iberists treat the peninsula as one natural unit separated by history, and 1580-1640 as a precedent; though the border was not drawn by an outside power.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not discussed; leading Iberists were intellectuals (Unamuno, Saramago).

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Iberism builds on respect for the peninsula's distinct cultures; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Not discussed; liberal and republican inference.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School curriculum on sexuality is outside Iberist sources.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Creationism teaching is not an Iberist topic; mild no inferred from the liberal strands.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Pornography law is not an Iberist topic.

minority-language-support.rationale: Íber's leader says linguistic diversity is no obstacle, citing Switzerland, and Catalan, Galician and Portuguese Iberism proposed a magazine in all peninsular languages (Maragall).

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for religious minorities are not an Iberist topic.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill-style nonconformity is not an Iberist topic.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Poor-country debt is not an Iberist topic; Mas did discuss public debts as a cost of Europe's wars, but not cancellation.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Iberism seeks to end the independence of two states rather than to deepen it, so the claim does not apply.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Federal republicans drew constitutions (Castelar's 1873 draft); inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Developmental authoritarianism is not an Iberist idea; its strands are liberal and democratic, so a mild no is inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid duties are not an Iberist topic.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear deterrence is not discussed; Mas wanted less militarisation, so a mild no is inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Republican Iberists would choose a head of state, but sources do not say how; the monarchist strand rejects election.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Íber proposes a joint Iberian Central Bank, but nothing is said about independence from government.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not discussed; Iberism has no territorial-peace dispute of this kind beyond Olivenza, which Portugal has not formally claimed.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Not discussed; liberal and social-federal strands would differ.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet debate is outside Iberism, apart from its anarchist wing, which was anti-Bolshevik.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk doctrine is not part of Iberism.

collective-defense.rationale: Mas wanted a single Iberian army and fleet; alliance doctrine is not discussed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Olivenza was taken by Spain in 1801 and Portugal has never formally claimed it; Iberists avoid the issue.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Liberal Iberists leaned anticlerical, conservative ones did not.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Mas envisaged a common crown; republican strands would want a president; no stance on neutrality is stated.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Mas insisted on peaceful and legal union; use of force to keep a region is not Iberist in spirit, though unstated.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Iberist designs are federal or confederal, with each nation keeping its own peculiarities (Íber) and Mas's plan keeping the two monarchies' political essence at first.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine kingship has no place in Iberism.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax-rate structure is not discussed in the sources read.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nature versus nurture is not discussed by Iberist sources.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Mas's union was to be constitutional and legal, and republican federalists built on pacts; absolutism is foreign.

space-expansion.rationale: Space is not an Iberist topic.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is not an Iberist theme.

leader-cult.rationale: Not discussed; cult regimes opposed Iberism.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not discussed by Iberist sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine foreign to Iberism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Federal republicans attacked latifundismo, but no Iberist-wide programme of redistribution exists.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not an Iberist topic.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Mas's plan added Andorra, Gibraltar and parts of France through union, not claims for a nationality abroad.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing apostasy is foreign to liberal and republican Iberism.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress mandates are foreign to Iberism.

common-currency.rationale: Mas explicitly proposed a single coin, metric system and commercial law for the whole peninsula, Latino Coelho wanted a single currency in a full zollverein, and Íber proposes a joint central bank.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Iberism's defining claim is that peoples with shared origin and near-identical language, Portuguese and Spaniards, should unite; Mas cites kinship and language, and pan-Iberism extends to Iberophone nations.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Catalan and Galician Iberists proposed a federation of nationalities that keep their own institutions, using Iberism against Castilian centralism.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The question of minority emigration is not part of Iberism.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Mas stressed material interests but not as a theory of history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is not addressed in the Iberist sources read.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not addressed in the Iberist sources read.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not covered in the Iberist sources.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Mas wanted open trade, not a closed bloc; his plan was framed partly to resist British and French commercial pressure but through merger and common tariffs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Linked trade standards are not covered in the Iberist sources, which only urge free commercial exchange.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moral incentives are a communist-state idea not found in Iberism.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foco theory is not part of Iberism, whose revolutionary wing was liberal-conspiratorial in the 1820s and anarchist later.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Republican strands opposed monarchy and aristocratic privilege, while monarchist Iberists did not; split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Curriculum framing is not covered by the Iberist sources.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mas wanted to develop both countries' colonies, but no doctrine of tutelage is stated.

patriotic-education.rationale: Not discussed; Iberist loyalty would be to a union.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: US-style affirmative action is not an Iberist topic.

public-money-creation.rationale: Public money creation is not discussed in the Iberist sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Crisis theory is not discussed in the Iberist sources.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The Lisbon Declaration speaks of an Iberophone community including Latin America, Lusophone countries and territories such as Philippines and Puerto Rico; Unamuno's cultural Iberism includes overseas peoples.

delink-world-market.rationale: Iberism is about integrating markets, and Mas wanted trade opened and colonies developed.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis not found in Iberism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian private discrimination is not discussed; mild no inferred from the liberal-social orientation.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional rights design is not detailed in the sources; Castelar's 1873 draft constitution may have included them but this was not read.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial borders are not an Iberist issue.

elective-rulers.rationale: Documented split: republican federal Iberists choose rulers by election, monarchist Iberists (Mas) keep a crown.

minority-veto.rationale: Not discussed; federal pacts differ from unanimity.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Liberal and republican Iberists were revolutionaries against absolutism (1820s secret societies); inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Constitutional and republican strands favour representative government; Mas pointed to representative government as excellent.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not an Iberist topic.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not an Iberist topic.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Aristocratic duty is not an Iberist theme; republican strands attacked privilege.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critical theory of mass culture is not an Iberist idea.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not an Iberist idea.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not Iberist; Mas was concerned with British commercial domination of Portugal but not with this thesis.

party-own-road.rationale: Intra-communist autonomy is not an Iberist matter.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development aid is not an Iberist topic.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Olivenza dispute is mentioned, but Portugal has never formally claimed it and Iberists seek union rather than territorial return.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous rule is not an Iberist topic.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Iberist currents were leftist, anarchist and republican, and Francoism and Salazarism opposed Iberism; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The equivalence of fascism and communism is not discussed in the sources read.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historiographic dispute outside Iberism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument politics are not covered by Iberist sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's issues are not covered by Iberist sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Iberist sources do not discuss whether Western institutions fit other civilisations.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Mas wanted to shrink the army; Iberist strands were liberal-civil.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care-work pay is not covered in Iberist sources.

filial-duty.rationale: Filial duty is not covered in Iberist sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service examination is not covered in Iberist sources.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Mas's common-market logic suggests openness within Iberia, but foreign takeover policy is not discussed.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not covered in the Iberist sources.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandate is not an Iberist demand, though Pi y Margall's pact federalism built power from the base.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not covered in the Iberist sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Occupancy-based land tenure is not an Iberist idea; a mild no is inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Constitutional and republican inference; not stated in the sources.

single-official-language.rationale: Iberism includes Catalan, Galician and Portuguese speakers; Íber's leader sees no problem with several languages, though Mas hoped for a near-common language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not discussed; Iberism would make peninsular nationals not foreigners to each other.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumerism critique is not an Iberist topic; Mas was a commercial optimist.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Mas's cause is peaceful and legal; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Intervention to keep allies in a bloc is not an Iberist idea; mild no inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying and campaign finance are not Iberist topics.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign NGO funding rules are not covered in the Iberist sources.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Natality policy is not covered in the Iberist sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property purchase limits are inconsistent with a peninsular common market, so a mild no is inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment guarantees are not covered in the Iberist sources.

democratic-peace.rationale: Mas argued that peaceful fusion of related peoples reduces wars and armies; he named Europe a republic of nations kept in peace by equilibrium.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: A philosophical-anarchist claim; liberal and republican Iberism accepts legal order, so a mild no is inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Mas wanted freedom from foreign meddling but not an absolute non-intervention principle; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not covered in the Iberist sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy thinking about minorities is alien to Iberism.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage law is not covered in the Iberist sources.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of information is not covered in the Iberist sources.

local-production.rationale: Mas's argument is for a broader peninsular market.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Iberists want deeper integration within the EU and between states; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Mas mentioned shared religion among reasons for union, but religion does not define the Iberist nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Mas denounced British and French dominance over Portugal and Spain.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not detailed in the sources; federal Iberism could go either way.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Socialist property distinctions are not covered in the Iberist sources.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anti-communism as a policy is not an Iberist concern; its anarchist and socialist wing would oppose it.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public service delivery is not covered in the Iberist sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: Religion as illusion is not an Iberist idea; Mas cited shared religion as a link.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Mas welcomed commerce, railways and industry but offers no theory.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not covered by the Iberist sources.

socialized-care.rationale: Not covered by the Iberist sources.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Iberists favour linguistic mixing and convergence of Spanish and Portuguese; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Indigenous treaties are not an Iberist topic.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small commune ideals are not core to Iberism, though the anarchist current (FAI) shares some of them.

majority-settlement.rationale: Majority settlement in minority regions contradicts Iberism's federal respect for nationalities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: A third-position slogan is not part of Iberism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Iberism cites history of the union of 1580-1640, but not as a claim over others' land.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial of the Holocaust has no basis in Iberist writing.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not covered by the Iberist sources; mild no from the liberal and left currents.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Authoritarian suppression was characteristic of the Estado Novo and Franco, regimes hostile to Iberism.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Blasphemy law is not covered by the Iberist sources; a mild no is inferred from the liberal strands.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Mas proposed developing the colonies, which suggests more than extraction, but he is not anti-colonial.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamist doctrine alien to Iberism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: An Islamist doctrine alien to Iberism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Pi y Margall's federalism built from municipalities up; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectionality is not an Iberist concept.

assisted-dying.rationale: Euthanasia law is not covered in Iberist sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Mas said his project served interests and not a party, but Iberism has mostly been placed on the left.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxian alienation is not an Iberist concept, though socialist Iberists might accept it.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not covered by Iberist sources; mild no because Iberism stresses shared culture across differences, though this is inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Not discussed; liberal and republican inference.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace-harassment law is not covered in Iberist sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Mas favoured open commerce and the social-federal wing favoured reform, but no source states a social-market synthesis.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Mas wanted a single army and fleet but much reduced; abolition not proposed.

rich-first.rationale: Deng-style gradualism is not an Iberist idea.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Modern Iberists want to stay in the EU; no stance on blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Mas's monarchist version supposed union through the royal houses; republican strands reject inheritance, so adherents split.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist credit is not covered in Iberist sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Mas decried public debt burdens, but refusing lender conditions is not discussed.

property-franchise.rationale: Democratic and republican strands wanted wide suffrage; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is not an Iberist idea.

reification.rationale: A Marxist-Lukacsian concept not found in Iberist sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A socialist critique of formal freedoms; only the socialist and anarchist Iberists would say it.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Mas wanted the union by legal means; inferred rule-of-law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Racial limits on voting are alien to Iberism.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic for the sources; modern Iberist groups organise online but state no doctrine.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data is not covered by Iberist sources.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Restricting mixed-faith marriage is alien to liberal Iberism; mild no inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Boycotts of minority shops are alien to Iberism.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are not part of the Iberist sources, which pre-date them.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is not covered by Iberist sources.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Republican federalists opposed latifundismo and oligarchy; others did not.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: State atheism is alien to Iberism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Abolitionism belongs at most to the anarchist fringe of Iberism, not its mainstream; mild no inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Iberist federal and confederal models share power among nationalities; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Charity versus state aid is not covered in Iberist sources.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not covered by Iberist sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not covered by Iberist sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is not an Iberist topic.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Marital law is not covered by Iberist sources.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Iberists want shared rights across the Spain-Portugal border; the 1931 Spanish constitution gave dual nationality to Portuguese residents.

rent-control.rationale: Housing-market policy is not covered by Iberist sources.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not covered in Iberist sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Uniformed youth movements are characteristic of the Salazar and Franco regimes, which opposed Iberism.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is not discussed by Iberist sources.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign basing is not discussed by Iberist sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Iberism's sources deal with national union, not discrimination law, so no lean can be documented.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Mas expected railways, canals and commerce to regenerate the peninsula, so he was optimistic about material progress, though he did not claim it solves everything.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Iberism takes no position; its federal-republican strands were progressive, so mild support is inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the mainstream view that self-defence is legitimate.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Iberists appeal to a shared peninsular history but do not claim an unbroken national identity from antiquity; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: A territorial project with no stated view on sex and gender; inferred as neutral.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Outside the movement's concerns; no position can be inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Iberism is a peaceful, legal union project with no martyr cult; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Its case is commercial, historical and constitutional, not a moral struggle; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Iberism seeks political union of the peninsula's states, the opposite of a homeland serving only as a cultural centre; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: The movement is primarily a constitutional and territorial project, putting political union first; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; the movement spans secular, republican and monarchist strands.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; no position can be inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Iberism favours merging markets and a single tariff across borders, which sits against ethnic economic reservation; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Iberism proposes merging Portugal and Spain, kindred peoples, into one political unit, which fits this statement loosely; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the progressive and federal-republican strands, which favoured free association; not a stated Iberist topic.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Iberism has no economic doctrine; the strands range from monarchist-fusionist to federal-republican.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the federal-republican strand's social reform leanings; unstated.

second-chamber.rationale: The monarchist and federal-republican strands differ on institutions, and the sources do not settle it.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from the mainly liberal, customs-union economics of Mas's plan; unstated.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Modern Iberists favour a confederation, and the federal-republican strand built unions from below through pacts.

family-wage.rationale: Not an Iberist topic; no commitment either way.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the liberal and federal-republican roots of 19th-century Iberism, which stressed individual rights.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Not an Iberist topic; no commitment either way.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Federal-republican Iberists such as Pi y Margall built federation on pacts between sovereign parts, so powers are not simply revocable by the centre.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Iberism rests on shared history and language and on peoples uniting, not on racial groups; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Not an Iberist topic; no commitment either way.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The movement sought union by peaceful agreement, as in the title of Mas's La Iberia: memoria sobre la conveniencia de la union pacifica.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Iberism grounds union in shared history and near-kindred languages, though Portuguese and Spanish remain separate, so the claim is only partly stated.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from its federal-republican and confederal schemes built on common citizenship; separate religious electorates are not discussed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Iberists sought a peaceful, legal union and talk of fear of Spanish annexation is on the Portuguese side, so the plot claim is not an Iberist theme; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Not an Iberist topic; mild support inferred from the progressive and federal-republican social-reform emphasis of its nineteenth-century figures.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic for the nineteenth-century movement and not addressed by modern Iberist parties; no clear stance follows.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the progressive reformist strand; the sources do not discuss duties to future generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and no Iberist position follows from the territorial project.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from Mas's case for peaceful union and a single state ending the frontier conflict, plus modern confederal Iberists inside the EU; arms policy is not stated.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; monarchist and republican strands would differ, so no stance is inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from Mas's customs and monetary union, which would remove barriers between the two countries; capital flows are not discussed directly.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: the project of a single peninsular state implies a single state armed force; the sources give no arms policy.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Iberism stressed a peaceful and legal union, but adherents did not take a stand on refusing orders; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the progressive and federal-republican strands' social reform stance; sources do not address bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the federal-republican social reform strand; not stated in the sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Iberism has no stated fiscal doctrine; Mas's plan was a customs and monetary union, which is not about borrowing rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as indifferent since Iberism concerns peninsular union rather than global economic order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Mas's plan sought a peaceful, legal union by agreement of existing governments, not destruction of the state; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Federal strands favoured local self-rule but the project is a single territorial union; the sources leave economic experimentation untouched.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is territorial and the sources say nothing on ecosystems.

sacred-nation.rationale: Iberism aims at a supranational union beyond the existing nations, so adherents are unlikely to sacralise either nation; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the progressive and federal-republican strands' social reform emphasis.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Catalan and Galician Iberists sometimes criticised Madrid centralism, but the sources give no colonial framing; inferred and split.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-republican humanist tradition of the 19th-century strands; not discussed in the sources.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the progressive and republican strands' support for public institutions and education.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Iberism is a territorial and constitutional project and takes no position; its strands range from Catholic monarchists to secular federal republicans.

farm-price-support.rationale: Iberism is indifferent on agricultural policy; the sources discuss customs and monetary union, not farm support.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Iberism is indifferent: neither Spain nor Portugal has nuclear weapons, and the movement has no defence doctrine on them.

workers-own-party.rationale: Split: federal-republican Iberists such as Pi y Margall had social-reform leanings, while monarchist-fusionist ones did not; the project itself is not about class parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred: modern Iberists work within the European Union's human-rights framework, and no strand would oppose such a ban.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the liberal and federal-republican tradition and the modern EU-oriented movement; the sources do not discuss it.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred: Catalan Iberists such as Maragall treated peninsular languages as kindred, and the movement stresses linguistic proximity, though it does not discuss this regional naming dispute.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Iberism takes no position on environmental regulation versus private liability.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: Iberists propose a confederal or federal state under modern constitutional government, with no role for customary chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Iberism is indifferent; nothing in the movement connects the union project to environmental priorities.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Iberism takes no position on sentencing policy.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Iberism takes no position; any union would involve several official languages, which makes a single national-language requirement unclear.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Iberism is a territorial project with no stated labour policy; indifferent.

voter-id.rationale: No stated position on voting rules; inferred as indifferent.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The federal-republican strand and modern confederalists favour secular states, though the monarchist strand does not address it; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Modern Iberists want union inside the EU's democratic framework, so a procedural view of democracy fits; inferred.

premarital-sex.rationale: Liberal and republican Iberists and today's confederal parties are socially liberal; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Iberists working inside the EU framework would not endorse shutdowns; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Iberism takes few economic positions; indifferent.

women-suffrage.rationale: Modern Iberist parties sit within European liberal-democratic norms, so equal political rights for women follow; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: No stated position, and adherents range across several traditions; neutral.

race-social-construct.rationale: Modern Iberists in a liberal EU setting would likely accept this; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Modern Iberists in an EU setting would accept equality agencies as normal; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Iberism has no land-ownership doctrine; the sources do not address homesteading.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from modern Iberists' orientation toward a European Union framework and law-based internationalism.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the federal-republican and progressive strands (Pi y Margall, Castelar), which were anticlerical rather than scriptural literalists.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the progressive federal-republican strands and present-day Iberist parties' reformist outlook; the sources do not address it directly.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: Iberism is a territorial project, and its liberal and federal-republican strands were not state-socialist.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the federal-republican strand's commitment to popular, representative politics; the sources do not discuss indirect election.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the federal-republican strand's secular outlook; the Catholic monarchist strand did not make a church privilege part of the project.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The federal-republican Iberists and Catalan Iberists such as Maragall wanted a federal peninsula in which historic nations keep self-government.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the peaceful, legal union Iberists propose, which is meant to rest on consent of both peoples rather than force.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The sources do not address colonial borders; Iberism concerns the Iberian peninsula only.

simple-living.rationale: Iberism has no position on lifestyle or self-sufficiency.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the movement's liberal, universalist outlook; the sources do not address indigenous settlement.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the progressive reformist strands; the sources do not address conscription.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: the sources frame Iberism through shared history and culture of the peninsula, with a cultural sense of peninsular peoples, but state no spiritual tie to land.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Mas's La Iberia argues for peaceful, legal union, and the federal-republican and present-day confederal strands stress law and constitutional means, so killing without trial conflicts with them.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred: Iberism is silent on China; its modern parties look to the European Union, and the sources give no position.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred: Iberists envisage uniting the two countries; kin minorities are not a theme in the sources.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the sources record no Iberist doctrine on resource ownership, and the strands split between monarchist and federal-republican social views.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the liberal nineteenth-century Iberists, such as the federal republicans, backed individual rights, though the sources do not address self-ownership.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: Iberism has no tax programme beyond a customs union, so no stand on consumption taxes is recorded.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: Iberism takes few social or economic positions, and the sources record no stand on targeted versus universal spending.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: the federal-republican and confederal strands work through parties and federal institutions, so bypassing them is unlikely.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred: Mas's argument for a single commercial territory and the liberal strand point to open markets, but the sources do not discuss privileges to firms.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred: the federal-republican strand and modern confederal Iberists lean toward a secular, non-confessional politics, though the sources do not say so.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: Iberism is a territorial project that takes no stand on technology and ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred: federal-republican and progressive Iberists generally supported liberal civil reform, though the sources do not discuss divorce.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred: Iberism takes no recorded stand on resource control, and a customs union of two countries would pool control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Iberism is a territorial project with no stated view on how wealth should be judged; adherents span monarchist and federal-republican strands, so neutral is inferred.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Modern Iberists want confederation inside the EU but the sources record no position on a financial transactions tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Iberism does not address racial disadvantage; no position is recorded, so neutral is inferred from its purely territorial focus.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The sources never discuss the authority of unjust law; neutral is inferred from the movement's silence.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Iberism is a nineteenth-century and territorial project that never addressed automation; neutral is inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Iberists favour a gradual confederation within the EU and a union of two states, inferred as a preference for larger integrated blocs over a world of separate power centres.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Iberism took no stand on value theory; Mas's economic proposals were about customs and currency union, so neutral is inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Iberists combined peninsular patriotism with differing social programmes; the sources record no link either way, so neutral is inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: Iberism is a constitutional project and its strands differ on social questions, so no position is recorded and neutral is inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The federal-republican and modern EU-oriented strands pursued union through democratic means, so a communist-party-led market is inferred to be foreign to them.

missingStatements.text: Neighbouring countries should abolish the customs barriers between them and form a customs union with a single tariff.
missingStatements.rationale: Mas's central economic argument is to end the frontier battle between tax officers and smugglers by joining the two countries into one commercial territory under a single tariff.

notes: The monarchist-fusionist (Mas, progresista liberals) and federal-republican (Pi y Margall, Garrido, Braga) strands differ on the form of government, and modern Iberists favour a confederation rather than a unitary merger, so regime-form statements are neutral. Pi y Margall's own federalism worked within Spain and Catalan sources treat it as distinct from Iberism. The sources read say little on economic redistribution or social issues, so most of those answers are low-confidence inferences. The Mas source was read in OCR text, not the original page images.
